title_original: Exclusive Poster for Xu Zao’s Acclaimed Debut Light Pillar, Opening This January

blocks.text: Premiering at the Berlinale earlier this year and subsequently playing at the Toronto International Film Festival, Pingyao International Film Festival (where it won Best Director), and more, Xu Zao’s directorial debut, the acclaimed animated feature Light Pillar, will now be arriving in U.S. theaters to kick off the New Year. We’re delighted to exclusively unveil the new poster, courtesy of Greenwich Entertainment, as well as a January 8 release date for the film that follows a janitor at a bankrupt movie studio who is drawn into a VR world, where a beautiful woman promises him a ticket to the moon if he can get her the money.

Here’s the full synopsis: “In the not-too-distant future, janitor Zha (Da Peng) tends the grounds of a bankrupt film studio, accompanied only by a cat who used to act in the studio’s movies. Unable to pay Zha’s salary, the studio’s owner offers him a virtual reality headset as partial compensation. Zha is soon drawn into a fantasy world, where he embarks on a romantic journey with a beautiful female player who promises him a ticket to the moon if he can get her the money for it. Set against the backdrop of a fading film industry, acclaimed animator Xu Zao makes a formally daring debut with Light Pillar , weaving hand-drawn animation and live action into a poignant meditation on one man’s search for belonging.”

“ Light Pillar is not hard-core science fiction, but is grounded in the daily life and struggles of our protagonist,” said Xu Zao. “When everyday life meets science fiction, comedy emerges naturally. It comes from what we perceive as normal, much like the strange humor of seeing a monkey type on a keyboard. About my style, this is not something I can change. I don’t think I deliberately pursue a specific style. Every decision in the creative process comes from the heart.”
